welcomeLine: Walk with me. We will begin with a story.
starLine: You have found Betelgeuse. Keep it in My sky to remember where to look.
endingLine: Your first star is in My sky. You can return to it whenever you like.
fact: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant: a reddish star much larger than the Sun. In Orion's star pattern, it marks one shoulder.

activity.prompt: Find the three stars that form Orion's belt.
activity.hint: Look for three bright stars close together, almost in a line.
activity.rightLine: You found the belt: three stars close together, almost in a line.
activity.showLine: Here is the belt. Look at these three close stars.
activity.explanation: These three stars form the belt in our picture of Orion.

groups.label: Group A
groups.description: Three widely spaced stars forming a triangle.
groups.missedLine: This group bends. Look for three stars almost in a line.

groups.label: Group B
groups.description: Three close stars in an almost-straight line.

groups.label: Group C
groups.description: Two far-apart stars with a third above them.
groups.missedLine: These stars are far apart. Look for three closer lights.

sources.title: NASA — Discovering the Universe Through Orion
